findings.title: `queued` default timestamp is fixed at import time
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once when the module is imported, not per instance. Every AssignmentSource created in a process therefore carries the same import-time timestamp, so `queued` is wrong for all real assignments. It is also serialized into `assignment_source_dict` and passed as Celery task kwargs, where every other value is a primitive. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` or drop the field if nothing reads it.

findings.title: New keyword is passed unconditionally to every integration's sync_assignee_outbound
findings.body: The task now always calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(external_issue, user, assign=assign, assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source)`, even when there is no source (None). Previously integrations only received `external_issue`, `user`, and `assign`. Any integration implementation that does not accept `**kwargs` will now raise TypeError on every outbound assignee sync, including ones unrelated to loop prevention. The only tests touching this path mock `sync_assignee_outbound`, so real implementation signatures are never exercised. Either verify that all implementations accept the kwarg, or pass it only when a source is present.

findings.title: Abstract sync_status_outbound gains an assignment_source parameter nothing uses
findings.body: The `assignment_source` parameter is added to the abstract `sync_status_outbound` contract, but no caller in this PR passes it and no implementation consumes it. Integrations reading this signature will assume the source is meaningful for status sync. The parameter is dead API surface and should be removed unless status sync is meant to honour the source in this change.

findings.title: from_dict silently returns None, which drops the loop guard
findings.body: `from_dict` swallows ValueError/TypeError and returns None without logging. Callers treat None as 'no assignment source', so the outbound sync propagates to every integration, including the one that originated the change, which is the exact loop this PR is meant to stop. An extra or renamed key in the dict (for example from a future schema change during a rolling deploy) would silently disable the guard. Log the failure or fail loudly.

findings.title: No test that other integrations still receive outbound updates when the source is a different integration
findings.body: The new test only checks that an assignment whose source matches the target integration is not propagated. The guard in `should_sync` is meant to block only the origin integration, with the comment saying 'This should still allow other integrations to propagate changes outward'. Nothing asserts that an assignment sourced from integration A still reaches a different linked integration B. An over-broad guard, such as one that skips all integrations whenever a source is set, would pass the current tests.

findings.title: Deassign path with a matching assignment source is not tested
findings.body: Unassignment from an inbound webhook also generates an outbound update, and the description names unassign as part of the loop. `sync_group_assignee_inbound` passes `assignment_source` to `deassign`, but no test checks that deassigning with a source matching the linked integration skips the outbound `sync_assignee_outbound` call. The only deassign test passes no source, so a regression in the deassign wiring would go unnoticed.
